name: BT2M-RerankBench
description: Although large language models (LLMs) have advanced the development of information retrieval technologies, their application is hindered by the issue of “hallucinations”. The retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture mitigates factual deviations by integrating retrievers, and can further incorporate rerankers, where rerankers significantly enhance query-document relevance matching through secondary semantic optimization of initial retrieval results. The study systematically reviews the evolution of reranking technology, categorizes it into three distinct stages, and identifies limitations in current reranker evaluation methods, specifically their singularity and lack of comprehensiveness. To this end, this paper proposes a novel comprehensive benchmark, BT2M-RerankBench, which innovatively constructs a comprehensive evaluation environment covering multilingual, multi-domain, and large-scale scenarios, and introduces a four-dimensional evaluation framework, overcoming the limitations of existing benchmarks with single metrics, and enhancing the comprehensiveness of reranker evaluation compared with traditional methods. In terms of dataset construction, this paper thoroughly surveys mainstream benchmarks widely recognized by the academic community in recent years to encure that the tests cover a wide range of fields and languages.
